skill.name: xlsx
skill.description: Create, edit, analyze, and validate spreadsheet files with guidance for pandas, openpyxl, formulas, formatting, and LibreOffice recalculation.
skill.summary: Guides spreadsheet creation, editing, data analysis, formula setup, and error checking for Excel workbooks.
skill.author: Cam10001110101

security_audit.summary: Most SKILL.md detections are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline code, formula error names, and examples. The real risks are in recalc.py, which installs a persistent LibreOffice macro and executes LibreOffice on user-selected workbooks. No evidence found of prompt injection text in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Do not silently write macros into the user profile. Require consent, document cleanup steps, and prefer a temporary or isolated macro location.

remediation.issue: External LibreOffice execution on workbook input
remediation.suggestion: Resolve trusted executable paths, validate workbook paths and extensions, process a temporary copy, and preserve strict timeouts.
Add file size limits, sheet or cell limits, and clear timeout handling before scanning every cell in large workbooks.

finding_verdicts.reason: This runs soffice with a fixed argument list to initialize LibreOffice, and no user data is passed to a shell. It is dependency setup rather than command injection.
This checks gtimeout --version with fixed arguments and captures output. There is no user-controlled command string or shell expansion.

This executes LibreOffice on a user-supplied workbook path and mutates the file through macro-based recalculation. The argument list avoids shell injection, but external office processing of untrusted files is a real risk.
The hardcoded URL is an XML namespace inside LibreOffice macro metadata. It is not used for an outbound network request.
The script targets a hidden LibreOffice profile directory under the user home. Writing persistent application macro files there is a sensitive filesystem change.
The code accesses the hidden LibreOffice configuration path to inspect or create macro content. This is intentional profile modification and should require clear consent.
The script writes Module1.xba into the LibreOffice macro directory. This persists executable macro behavior outside the workbook being processed.
The script creates the LibreOffice macro directory under the user profile. This is expected for the helper, but it is still a persistent filesystem modification.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent LibreOffice Macro Installation
semantic_findings.description: The helper creates Module1.xba under the user LibreOffice profile and writes a RecalculateAndSave macro. Persistent application macros should require explicit consent and cleanup guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setup function builds a user profile macro path and writes Module1.xba when the macro is missing. This confirms persistent macro installation beyond the target workbook.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Workbook Cell Scanning

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet work often needs formulas, formatting, and checks that preserve workbook behavior. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Excel creation, editing, analysis, and formula validation.
actual_capabilities: Creates new .xlsx workbooks with formulas, formatting, sheets, and column widths.
Reads and analyzes Excel, CSV, and TSV data with pandas workflows.
Edits existing workbooks while preserving formulas and formatting through openpyxl guidance.
Recalculates formulas through the included LibreOffice-based recalc.py helper.
Reports formula errors such as #REF!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, and #NAME?.
Provides financial model formatting and source documentation conventions.
limitations: Formula recalculation depends on LibreOffice being available in the runtime.
The helper script writes a LibreOffice macro into the user LibreOffice profile.
Large workbooks can be slow because the helper scans all cells.
It does not replace manual review of business logic, assumptions, or source data.

use_cases.title: Build a reporting workbook
use_cases.description: Create a formatted workbook with formulas, source notes, and validation checks for recurring reports.

use_cases.title: Update a financial model
use_cases.description: Modify an existing model while preserving formulas, styles, assumptions, and workbook structure.

use_cases.title: Analyze spreadsheet data
use_cases.description: Load Excel or CSV data, summarize columns, and export a clean workbook for review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excel workbook for quarterly sales tracking. Include input rows, summary formulas, clear headers, and simple formatting.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an existing file
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the attached spreadsheet. Summarize key columns, identify missing values, and suggest workbook improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Edit and preserve formulas
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this workbook with a new scenario sheet. Preserve existing formatting, formulas, and sheet structure wherever possible.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a financial model
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this financial model for formula errors, broken references, formatting consistency, and source documentation gaps.

output_examples.input: Create a monthly budget workbook with income, expenses, and savings formulas.
output_examples.output: A formatted workbook with monthly tabs, totals, variance formulas, highlighted assumptions, and a summary sheet.

output_examples.input: Check this workbook after adding new formulas.
output_examples.output: A validation summary that lists formula error types, affected cells, total formulas, and recommended fixes.

output_examples.input: Analyze this sales spreadsheet and prepare a cleaner version.
output_examples.output: A cleaned workbook with typed columns, summary tables, basic charts, and notes about missing or inconsistent data.

best_practices: Keep formulas in the workbook so users can update source data later.
Recalculate and validate formula results before delivering important files.
Document hardcoded assumptions with clear source notes and dates.
anti_patterns: Do not replace formulas with static values unless the user requests it.
Do not ignore formula errors after modifying workbook structure.
Do not change established template formatting without a clear reason.

faq.question: Can this skill create new Excel files?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides workbook creation with sheets, formulas, formatting, and saved .xlsx files.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing workbook?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends openpyxl workflows that preserve formulas and formatting when used carefully.

faq.question: Does it recalculate formulas?
faq.answer: Yes, through recalc.py and LibreOffice. This requires LibreOffice and may modify the workbook.

faq.question: Can it analyze CSV or TSV files?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance includes pandas workflows for Excel, CSV, and tabular data.

faq.question: Does it validate formula errors?
faq.answer: It can scan recalculated workbooks for common Excel errors and report affected cells.

faq.question: Is manual review still needed?
faq.answer: Yes. Review assumptions, source data, and business logic before using important workbooks.
